doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Jimmy Garrison's last visit and the Vienna anthem
summary: Elvin recalls Garrison's last request for money and his wife, and the Vienna request to play the national anthem.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: So of course Eric went in ’64 but then Jimmy.

Jimmy came here. He called up Keiko and asked, this is just before he died, he said, “I need $150.” So she wrote a check and we said we’d leave it with the doorman. So he says, “Okay.” I know the check was gone and I didn’t see Jimmy again. Somebody picked it up. That’s strange because his wife, Roberta, her father was one of the wealthiest doctors in San Francisco, I mean rich! She had stocks, and bonds, and all kinds of stuff. (Laughs) And she had him put in jail for child support! That’s mean, that’s cruel. (Laughs) She came to the funeral with some red slacks. It was sort of disgraceful in some sort of way, everyone else was trying to pay their respects. You know I’ll tell you a story that happened to us with Joe Farrell and Jimmy went on one of our European trips. And this was in Vienna. So the guy says, “You know we want you, and your trio to come”, it was Johann Strauss’ birthday or death, or something “So we want you to go to the statue and play the national anthem.” (Laughs) So I go to Jimmy and I say, “You know the national anthem don’t you?” (Laughs) He said, “No!” and neither did Joe. So we started playing it and Joe said (Elvin scats a melody vaguely resembling of the national anthem) (Laughs). That was funny, that day.
So that was a very special group for you then.
Oh yeah, never a dull moment.
